questions.question: Describe one hard engineering strategy used to protect the coast. (2 marks)

points.text: Rock armour involves placing large boulders (1-2 tonnes) at the base of cliffs (1 mark). The boulders absorb and deflect wave energy, reducing erosion of the cliff behind (1 mark).

questions.question: Explain how groynes protect the coastline. (4 marks)

points.text: Groynes are wooden or concrete barriers built at right angles to the coastline, extending into the sea (1 mark). They trap sediment being transported by longshore drift on the up-drift side (1 mark). This builds up a wider beach which absorbs more wave energy naturally (1 mark). questions.question: Compare hard and soft engineering approaches to coastal management. (6 marks)

points.text: Hard engineering uses artificial structures to resist wave energy - sea walls reflect waves and prevent flooding, but are expensive (£5,000-10,000/m) and ugly (1 mark). Rock armour and gabions absorb energy but have shorter lifespans (1 mark). questions.question: Using a named UK coastline, assess the effectiveness of coastal management strategies. (9 marks)

points.text: The Holderness Coast in East Yorkshire is Europe's fastest-eroding coastline, retreating at 1.8 m/year. At Hornsea, hard engineering including a sea wall, rock armour and groynes has effectively protected the town (1 mark).
